title: Commercial hotel work in 1980
summary: He plays accompaniment six nights a week and says he has paid his dues twice.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: You are, as much as anybody, based and founded in the "real jazz era," the developmental era and you're still working commercial gigs six nights a week in March--where are we, the twenty fourth, twenty third, 1980. With everything else you've stretched across an awful lot and you are playing material now that you never thought you'd be playing. Talk about that.
I've done this in my past and as I explained before it's just the level in work that I've come back to since starting at the beginning.
You've paid your dues and you're well back from--
Talk about your relationship between this music and the music that you were inventing some years ago.

The commercial music that I'm involved with now in our job? It's just that, it's my job, it consists of accompaniment mostly, or fifty percent of it is accompanying singers, acts, playing their material for them. What makes it interesting is that the shows are different every night, but then again many of the acts repeat. There is an aura of repetition about it.
This is going nowhere--strike that. I was searching for something.
I'll be damned if I know.
The job is nothing, it's leading nowhere.
